objective: Configure key-based SSH login with ssh-keygen and ssh-copy-id
secondaryObjectives: List listening ports and the processes behind them with ss
Copy files between machines with scp, sftp and rsync

sources.cite: inode(7), file mode bits: set-group-ID and sticky bit (man7.org, man-pages 6.19)
sources.note: Relevant text: 'For newly created files, the file group ID is either the group ID of the parent directory or the effective group ID of the creating process, depending on whether or not the set-group-ID bit is set on the parent directory'; 'The sticky bit (S_ISVTX) on a directory means that a file in that directory can be renamed or deleted only by the owner of the file, by the owner of the directory, and by a privileged process.' The organization, the systems, the data and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You are setting up web02 for Ferngrove Bakery's online shop, a fictional small business. The server is on the internet with password SSH login enabled. You need to log in securely, check what's listening, and copy the site from web01.
handover: web02: fresh install, root login and password authentication allowed.
The site is 3 GB on web01 under /var/www/shop.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the map shows each component and its status in words.
Move on a check-in at a time. A decision comes to you at each check-in; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

then.log: Check-in 2: no one can log in over SSH; the fix takes an hour through the hosting panel's slow console.
Check-in 3: an internet scanner finds the open Redis and overwrites a key the shop uses for cart prices.
Check-in 4: the admin password, sent in clear over FTP, is reused in a login attempt on web01 from an unknown address.

keysPrompt.title: Passwords under attack
keysPrompt.context: You have console access through the hosting panel as a fallback.

choices.label: ssh-keygen an ed25519 key with a passphrase, ssh-copy-id it to your admin account, confirm a key login works in a second session, then set PasswordAuthentication no and PermitRootLogin no and reload sshd

effects.log: Key login works; passwords and root login are off.

choices.feedback: Test the key in a second session before turning passwords off, so you never lock yourself out.

choices.label: Add your key but leave password login on

effects.log: Your key works; passwords stay on.

choices.feedback: You're safer, but the guessing against passwords continues.

choices.label: Turn off password login first, then sort out keys

effects.log: Password login is turned off first.

choices.feedback: With no key installed, the reload locks every admin out over SSH.

redisPrompt.title: Redis open to the internet
redisPrompt.context: The shop connects to Redis on the same host.

choices.label: Set Redis to bind 127.0.0.1 with protected mode on, restart it, and confirm with ss -tlnp that it listens only on localhost
choices.feedback: ss shows the address a service listens on; local-only services bind to localhost.

choices.label: Block 6379 in the host firewall but leave the bind
choices.feedback: Blocked for now, but one firewall change re-exposes it.

choices.label: Leave it: the shop works
choices.feedback: An unauthenticated Redis on the internet is quickly abused.

copyPrompt.title: 3 GB from web01
copyPrompt.context: The copy may be interrupted; permissions and timestamps matter to the web server.

choices.label: rsync -a over SSH from web01 to web02 (archive mode keeps permissions and times, and a rerun copies only what's missing), then compare with a dry run

effects.log: The site is copied and verified.

choices.feedback: rsync over SSH is encrypted, preserves attributes and resumes efficiently.

choices.label: scp -r the whole directory
choices.feedback: Encrypted, but an interruption restarts from zero and some attributes aren't kept.

choices.label: Install an FTP server on web02 and upload with the admin password
choices.feedback: FTP sends the password and files unencrypted and opens another internet-facing service.

reflection.question: Write the setup notes: how you secured SSH, what ss showed, and how the site was copied.

scoring.modelReasoning: ssh-keygen creates a key pair and ssh-copy-id installs the public key; test the key in a second session before setting PasswordAuthentication no and PermitRootLogin no. ss -tlnp lists listening sockets and their processes, showing services bound to all interfaces that should be local only. rsync -a over SSH copies encrypted, keeps permissions and times, and resumes; plain FTP sends credentials in clear.
